annotatedSteps.description: Identification of the phenomenon splitting white light into colours
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Refraction is the bending of light; the splitting into colours is called dispersion of light.

annotatedSteps.description: Reason for obtaining a spectrum of seven colours
annotatedSteps.studentWork: (b) Different colours of light bend through different angles with respect to the incident ray as they pass through the prism, so they get separated.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correctly stated reason for separation into seven colours.

annotatedSteps.description: Ray diagram representing the internal phenomena in a raindrop
annotatedSteps.studentWork: [Draws circular raindrop with incident ray, refraction, dispersion, internal reflection, and emerging rays]
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct path showing entry, dispersion, internal reflection, and emergence.

annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Key stages labelled, but ray arrows are entirely missing and emerging rays are inverted (red emerges above violet).
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Add arrows showing the direction of light rays; the upper emerging ray should be labelled 'red' and the lower 'violet'.

teacherNote: Well-attempted explanation for part (b) and a neat diagram. Be careful with definitions: splitting of white light into constituent colours is 'dispersion', not 'refraction'. Also ensure all optical ray diagrams include directional arrows and accurate emerging colour positions.

rubric.point: (a) Naming the phenomenon as dispersion of light
(b) Stating the reason: different colours bend through different angles / travel at different speeds
(c) Ray diagram showing refraction, dispersion, and internal reflection in a water droplet
(c) Complete and correct labelling with directional arrows on rays
